decompileLimit: Il2CppInterop stub assemblies carry metadata, field and method signatures, and CallerCount/CachedScanResults attributes, but no method bodies: every body is an il2cpp_runtime_invoke trampoline. Caller counts and RVA ranges below are the interop metadata's own, not a decompiled call graph. Anything that would require a body (which field a method writes, whether a synced path runs on the host) is marked unverified rather than guessed.

hostClientVisibility.question: can the host see a client's reload start edge?
hostClientVisibility.answer: not established by this evidence; the adapter publishes only what the machine it runs on can read back
reasoning: The reload state on this build is a local field pair: Player.ItemEquippable.IsReloading with its backing field, and Player.PlayerInventorySynced.m_equipStatus whose enum has a Reload member. Both are ordinary fields with no reader declared in the interop metadata.
The one item-status packet the base class declares (pSimpleItemSyncData) carries inAimMode, inFireMode and inCooldown only, so it cannot be the reload edge.
PlayerInventorySynced declares no TriggerReload and no DoReload override, so there is no synchronised reload method to hook on the receiving machine.
Therefore whether a client's reload reaches the host at all is a runtime question this slice cannot answer statically. Guessing it either way would put an unverified claim in the contract.

Consequence, stated as the rule the implementation follows: the four reload facts are published from the machine that runs the reload, and every fact is read back from state on that machine. No fact is synthesised on a machine that cannot read the state behind it.
hostClientVisibility.sameShapeAs: The already shipped weapon and deployable families take the same position: WeaponNativeHooks patches the unsynced Fire body and the Synced Fire body separately, because neither reaches the other.

derivation.reload_started: ItemEquippable.set_IsReloading with a true value, or PlayerInventoryBase.TriggerReload, opens one reload life for that equipment entity. The first of the two to arrive opens it; a second does not publish again, so one reload has one started fact.
derivation.reload_transferred: The clip read back from ItemEquippable.GetCurrentClip() on the machine's own inventory is compared with the clip the open reload life recorded when it opened. A positive difference is the amount that actually entered the magazine; that difference is published once and the life's baseline is moved forward, so a second readback of the same difference publishes nothing.
derivation.reload_completed: The IsReloading edge back to false closes the open life. A life that transferred at least one round publishes its final amount as completed; a life that transferred nothing falls through to cancelled. one readback, one fact.
derivation.reload_cancelled: Closing a life that moved no ammunition is a reload that ended without a transfer. The reason code is 'unobserved': the game records no cause on any member this decompile exposes, so 'switched-weapon', 'downed' and 'damaged' would be invented distinctions. The decomposition of the reason is the place a later slice with real evidence should widen this row.
derivation.refilled_relationship: reload_transferred is a magazine gain taken from the player's own pack during one open reload life. The pack-side gains a refill produces (PickupAmmo, FillAllClips, SetStorageData, InitialReloadOfAllWeapons) are not a reload_transferred: they are the ammunition-pool family's readback, shared with ammo_changed, and they carry the refill source instead. One readback is never published twice.

unverified: Whether PlayerInventorySynced.m_equipStatus ever reads Reload on a non-owning machine (needs a live two-machine check).

The return semantics of TryTriggerReloadAnimationSequence and TryStartAnimationSequenceCoroutine: the stubs carry no body, so 'false' is not documented as a refusal here and no fact is published from those return values.
Whether a host-side write reaches PlayerInventoryLocal or PlayerInventorySynced for a remote player's reload; the adapter patches the base class once so both overrides are covered either way.
